TOP: Abandoned ASP.NET library exploited for unauthenticated RCE
Hijacked npm packages drive 99% of malware downloads
OpenAI and Cisco ship Shirudo live shields

P.h: Abandoned ASP.NET anti-CSRF library exploited for unauthenticated RCE, no patch coming
P.p: Attackers are exploiting a critical insecure deserialization flaw (CVSS 9.3) in Idunno.AntiCsrf, an ASP.NET WebForms library abandoned since 2008. One unauthenticated POST with a Base64 ObjectStateFormatter gadget chain gives code execution as w3wp.exe. Mandiant found the bug and confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
P.s: No fix exists for versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta. Search Web.config and bin/ for AntiCsrfModule, replace it with System.Web.Helpers.AntiForgery or ASP.NET Core IAntiforgery, and rotate machineKey and secrets if IIS logs show odd .aspx POSTs returning 302 or 500.

items.d: An attacker took data from the KEPCO ON customer portal and supplier platform: 650,487 customers with bank and card details, plus 869,761 supplier and employee records. Services were suspended.

items.h: Inception extortion crew claims seven victims in a week
items.d: New leak-site brand, possibly a ShinyHunters reboot, listed AMD, Cigna, PepsiCo, AutoZone, Lucid and two others.

items.h: Turnitin discloses cyberattack on customer-facing systems
items.d: Used by 16,000+ institutions. Scope and access method undisclosed. Watch for Turnitin-themed phishing and review SSO and LMS integration logs.
Attackers took over Workday accounts and changed direct-deposit details within seconds, using scripted browser steps with fixed two-second pauses. TLDR IT carries it too.

P.h: 5,400 malicious npm packages: hijacked legit packages drive nearly all the downloads
P.p: A Databricks review of about 5,400 malicious npm packages found compromised legitimate packages were only 7% of the set but over 99% of downloads. After npm revoked long-lived tokens, attackers moved to compromising CI pipelines and publishing through OIDC trusted publishing.
P.s: 38% of packages hid C2 traffic in services like Cloudflare Workers and Discord webhooks. The registry took a median of 7 days to remove malware. Harden CI pipelines, not just tokens.

items.h: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, an eBPF live-shield runtime
items.d: Open source (BSD 2-Clause). Temporary signed shields block a vulnerable code path on a running Linux host with no restart or patch. In one demo a Codex-made shield stopped a Java4Shell exploit. InfoSec, IT and DevOps all cover it.

items.h: AWS WAF now finds and guards LLM, MCP and A2A endpoints
items.d: Flags undocumented public MCP servers as shadow APIs and adds a managed rule group plus Bedrock Guardrails against prompt injection. Content inspection costs extra.

items.h: AI agents create a shared responsibility gap
items.d: MCP spec and agent harnesses leave audit logging and sensitive-action duty with the user. Agents need owners, least privilege and consistent logs.

items.h: Google warns autonomous AI cyberattacks are here
items.d: Attackers automate parts of intrusions with AI agents, raising pressure on patching and incident response.

P.h: Microsoft declares 'Code Red' after a 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage
P.p: Internal memos show Microsoft overhauling engineering and incident response after the 24-hour outage earlier this month. It targets worldwide recovery within one hour for future incidents, with better traffic isolation, patch deployment and diagnostics.
P.s: InfoWorld says the outage exposed hidden cloud dependencies even in locally installed software, so continuity plans should test whole business processes against vendor outages.
